text:
[IRET.12.2] **Justification withdrawal.** The engine must retract exactly the
logical facts [LLOG.2.5] leaves unsupported: a logical fact survives while it
has a well-founded justification, one that does not rest on the fact itself.

On every program [LCYC.3.1.1] admits, support is acyclic — no SCC both emits
and matches a schema — so a count of live justifications decides it, and libds
maintains one. When an activation ends (its token is retracted because a
supporting fact in the LHS was retracted or a NOT condition became
unsatisfied):

1. Look up all logical facts this activation supports in
   the dependency table.
2. For each: decrement `justif_count`.
3. For each where `justif_count == 0`: retract the fact
   from working memory (generating a `fact_retract`
   stream event). The retraction may cascade through the
   Rete network if other rules pattern-match on F.
4. Remove the activation's entry from the dependency
   table.

**An activation can end inside its own firing** ([LLOG.15.1]), when an
action of the firing retracts a fact its token holds. The steps run at that
action, and the firing goes on. The engine must not enter a logical fact the
firing asserts after that action in the dependency table against the ended
activation. It must retract that fact as it is asserted, unless another live
justification already holds it.

**The clock tick's turnover ends no match.** The tick is not a supporting
fact: a match that persists across ticks is one match ([IRET.19.5]), so the
engine must not run these steps when the only change to its token is the tick.
The activation formed again with the new tick takes over the justifications of
the one the tick's retraction removed (`carry_across_tick`, `terminal.c`). The activation ends, and its justifications are withdrawn, on the tick at
which its time-dependent test goes false ([LTIM.2.7.2]).

**The count is correct only because support is acyclic.** On a support cycle
it keeps every member's count above zero with no well-founded justification
left, and [LLOG.2.5] retracts them. So admitting emit-and-read cycles — the
shape a `+recursive` admission would license — requires replacing the count
with a mechanism that finds unfounded sets, and must not land without one.

alloy.name: iret_12_2__admitted_support_acyclic
alloy.note: The clause's sentence 'on every program [LCYC.3.1.1] admits, support is acyclic' as a bounded check: under condition (a) of the admission -- no kind both emitted and matched within one SCC of the emit-edge rule graph -- no fact lies in its own ancestor cone of the firing-level support relation. The direct statement at scope 4; at scope 6 through the model's two cheaper checks, the kind graph acyclic and support projecting onto it, which compose into it. The condition is needed: probe__unadmitted_cycle exhibits a support cycle without it.

alloy.name: iret_12_2__retract_iff_no_justifier
alloy.note: A snapshot of the refcount: a logical fact is live iff some justifier is. Well-founded support ([LLOG.2.5]) is the contract, and this clause's count is a mechanism that must agree with it. The two coincide on every program [LCYC.3.1.1] admits (acyclic support: formal/idris/Rete/Refcount.idr, iret_12_3__ranked_agree) and differ on an unfounded cycle (iret_12_2__witness_refcount), which no admitted program reaches. So this check is the clause on the admitted fragment and less than the clause in general: partial, not violated.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_after_gone_shape
idris.note: The end of a phase, with the retracted ids named: nothing, or their retraction and its propagation.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_gone_shape
idris.note: What a phase does to the core state, with the retracted ids named: nothing, or the retraction of the zeroed targets of the ended rows and its propagation.

idris.name: iret_12_2__reach_engine_cascade
idris.note: Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade on the engine's own table is the engine's final working memory: both Reach facts kept. `iret_12_2__cascade_unfounded` then says they are an unfounded set, in the engine.

idris.name: iret_12_2__reach_engine_run
idris.note: Executed: the seed's withdrawal ends its activation, Reach(1,2) drops to one justification and is kept -- step 3 retracts nothing, and the cycle survives.

idris.name: iret_12_2__ended
idris.note: Step 1 for every ending at once: the rows whose activation is no longer live. A row whose target is already gone is dropped with them, which is what keeps the model total when [LLOG.11.8] is violated.

idris.name: iret_12_2__kept
idris.note: The rows still live after the endings.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase
idris.note: The cascade to its fixpoint with one more phase than there are rows: a phase that changes anything drops a row.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_after
idris.note: The end of a phase that ended something: nothing to retract and only the table changes, or the retraction and its propagation. Split out so the bridge's proofs can case on it.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_empty
idris.note: An empty table ends nothing, so a phase on it is the identity.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n
idris.note: The phases iterated, each result taken apart and rebuilt so a run evaluates once per step.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step
idris.note: One cascade phase: drop the ended rows, retract what they alone supported, propagate. Breadth-first over every ending at once, where the clause and [IRET.7.8] describe a depth-first cascade one fact at a time; the fixpoint is the same because a retraction creates no positive match and only drops or unblocks tokens, but that equivalence is argued in the header, not proved.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids
idris.note: Step 3: retract those facts from working memory.

idris.name: iret_12_2__zeroed
idris.note: Steps 2-3: the ended rows' targets whose count against the remaining rows is zero.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__do_action_tms_net_elem
idris.note: What one action with truth maintenance leaves live: live before, or minted by the action; the cascade only removes.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__do_action_tms_net_keeps
idris.note: One action with truth maintenance keeps what is carried: the dispatch, the record (rows alone), the cascade.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__phase_n_net_keeps
idris.note: Phases keep what is carried. By induction on their number.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__phase_net_keeps
idris.note: The cascade to its fixpoint keeps what is carried.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__phase_net_sub
idris.note: The cascade only removes, at the fixpoint's fuel: Rete/NetworkWindowLapse.idr's.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__phase_step_net_keeps
idris.note: One phase keeps what is carried: it ends nothing, or it retracts the zeroed ids.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__sweep_ids_net_keeps
idris.note: A correlation sweep keeps what is carried: the retraction of ids and the cascade.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2__sweep_ids_net
idris.note: The sweep on the clocked network: the ids retracted one at a time through alpha dispatch, then the cascade; nothing to sweep is the identity.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2__sweep_ids_net_sub
idris.note: A SWEEP ONLY REMOVES: a fact live after it was live before, over every id list and state.

idris.name: iret_12_2__ended_net_ext
idris.note: The rows a phase ends depend on the chains' activations alone.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_view
idris.note: Any number of phases keep the view.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net_view
idris.note: The cascade to its fixpoint keeps the view.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_view
idris.note: One phase keeps the view.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_view
idris.note: The cascade's retractions, one fact at a time by id, keep the view.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__no_cascade_is_the_retime
idris.note: A cascade that finds no ended row touches nothing, by the quiet case of the phase.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__rows_live
idris.note: What the clause's cascade leaves at its fixpoint: every surviving row's target is live.

idris.name: Ltim_2_5_1__tms_inv_live
idris.note: The state between the clause's cascades: the invariant, and every row's target live.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_ttl
idris.note: The clause's cascade, however many times the other rules' endings start it inside the run, never touches a framed chain: its targets are emitted kinds.

idris.name: iret_12_2__fixed_rows_live
idris.note: At the fixpoint every row's target is live.

idris.name: iret_12_2__kept_net_sub
idris.note: The rows a phase keeps are rows it started with.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_fixed
idris.note: THE FUEL ON THE NETWORK: with at least as many phases as rows, the cascade reaches a phase that ends nothing, since every other phase drops a row. Rete/TmsBridge.idr's `iret_12_2__phase_n_fixed` for the network's phase, which retracts one fact at a time. What makes `rows_live` hold between actions, so that no stale row survives to a mint.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_frame
idris.note: Phases iterated skip a framed chain.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_inv
idris.note: Phases iterated keep the invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_stable
idris.note: Nothing ending, nothing changes however many phases run.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_unfired
idris.note: Any number of phases keeps every activation unfired when all were.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net_frame
idris.note: THE CLAUSE'S CASCADE SKIPS A FRAMED CHAIN. A CASCADE'S TARGETS ARE EMITTED KINDS: a row is recorded by a logical emit and targets the fact that emit left live, so what a cascade retracts is of a kind some rule of the program emits, which under the frame no framed chain reads.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net_inv_live
idris.note: The clause's cascade, run to its fixpoint, keeps the invariant and leaves every row's target live.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net_unfired
idris.note: The cascade keeps every activation unfired when all were.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_frame
idris.note: One phase of the clause's cascade skips a framed chain. A CASCADE'S TARGETS ARE EMITTED KINDS: a row is recorded by a logical emit and targets the fact that emit left live, so what a cascade retracts is of a kind some rule of the program emits, which under the frame no framed chain reads.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_inv
idris.note: One phase of the clause's cascade keeps the invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_shape
idris.note: A phase on the network either ends nothing and is the identity, or keeps strictly fewer rows.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_unfired
idris.note: One phase keeps every activation unfired when all were.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_frame
idris.note: The cascade's retractions skip a chain that reads none of the retracted kinds.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_inv
idris.note: The cascade's retractions, each of a live fact, keep the frame invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_sub
idris.note: The cascade's retractions only remove facts.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_unfired
idris.note: Retracting ids keeps every activation unfired when all were: it only retracts, and a retraction fires nothing.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_unique
idris.note: The cascade's retractions keep ids unique.

idris.name: iret_12_2__zeroed_target
idris.note: Step 3: the ids retracted are targets of rows the phase started with.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__entity_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE ENTITY STATE: A fires for the replacement's match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent; the entity and the input relation, which no row targets, are left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: The theorem at the fixture: A's firings are its matches, 1, with the clause's cascade inside the run. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_trace_ttl
idris.note: The clause's cascade, executed inside A's run: B's withdrawal ends its activation and the kind-2 fact it had just recorded is retracted; no kind-2 fact survives its justifier.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_b_first
idris.note: B's withdrawal of its own matched fact ends the activation that recorded its kind-2 row, so the clause's cascade retracts the kind-2 fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ticked_trace_ttl
idris.note: THE TRACE FROM THE TICKED STATE: A fires for the surviving match, B fires and cascades, `[1, 0]`, quiescent, the kind-0 fact alone left live. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_is_an_instance_ttl
idris.note: The theorem at the two-fact fixture: A's firings are its matches, 2, with the clause's cascade between them. Executed.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_facts_run_ttl
idris.note: The clause's cascade twice inside one run, each firing a `Refl` from a literal state: B's withdrawal ends its activation and the kind-2 fact it had recorded is retracted, between A's two firings and after the second. The literal after each cascade holds no kind-2 fact and no row.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_tms
idris.note: Kind 2 is a relation so that B's emit records a row for the cascade to act on. A fixture.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_clocked
idris.note: The clause's cascade, inside the run and after every prepare, never touches a framed chain: its targets are emitted kinds.

idris.name: iret_19_5__retime_clocked_inv
idris.note: The clause's cascade after a re-time keeps the invariant and leaves every row's target live.

idris.name: iret_19_5__retime_clocked_unfired
idris.note: The clause's cascade after a re-time fires nothing.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__ended_fired_cascade
idris.note: The clause's cascade executed after a re-time with a row to drop: the row goes and its target is retracted.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__gated_trace
idris.note: The clause's cascade executed inside A's run after the edge: B's withdrawal ends its activation and the kind-2 fact it had recorded is retracted.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_b_shutting
idris.note: B records a row and keeps its match, so a tick, not its own withdraw, is what ends the activation. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_gated
idris.note: B's withdrawal of its own matched fact ends the activation that recorded its kind-2 row, so the clause's cascade retracts the kind-2 fact. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__rules_shutting
idris.note: The same two rules under the shutting gate. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_b_shutting
idris.note: Kind 2 is a relation, so the row exists for the tick's cascade to drop. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_gated
idris.note: Kind 2 is a relation so that B's emit records a row for the cascade to act on. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_shutting
idris.note: Kind 2 is a relation, as in the opening fixture. A fixture.

idris.name: ltim_2_8_4__arrives_open_trace
idris.note: The clause's cascade executed inside A's run: B's withdrawal ends its activation and the kind-2 fact it had recorded is retracted.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__entry_retime_untimed
idris.note: The cascade from a state with no ended row is the identity: Rete/TmsRun.idr's fixpoint, which the cascade after every action and every input reaches.

idris.name: iret_12_2__ended_agree
idris.note: The rows that ended agree.

idris.name: iret_12_2__ended_net
idris.note: The rows whose activation has ended, or whose target is no longer live -- read off the terminals.

idris.name: iret_12_2__kept_agree
idris.note: The rows kept agree.

idris.name: iret_12_2__kept_net
idris.note: The rows still live, read off the terminals.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net
idris.note: Iterate, rebuilding the state each phase as FireLoopTms does.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_succ
idris.note: One more phase on the network, when the first is known.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_net
idris.note: The cascade to its fixpoint, with FireLoop's fuel: one more than the number of rows.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_cons
idris.note: A phase on FireLoop that ends something keeps the live rows and retracts what the ended ones alone supported, as a batch.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net
idris.note: One phase on the network: drop the rows of ended activations, retract what they alone supported, one fact at a time. A phase that ends nothing touches nothing.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_cons
idris.note: A phase on the network that ends something keeps the live rows and retracts what the ended ones alone supported.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_nil
idris.note: A phase on the network that ends nothing is the identity.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net
idris.note: Retract the facts with those ids one at a time through alpha dispatch, as the reference engine cascades; an id no live fact carries is skipped.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_wm
idris.note: Retracting ids one at a time leaves the working memory the batch leaves, under unique ids.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__phase_agree
idris.note: THE CASCADE AGREES: with the same rows on both sides the fuel is the same, and every phase agrees.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__phase_n_agree
idris.note: Any number of phases agree.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__phase_step_agree
idris.note: ONE PHASE AGREES: the two sides end and keep the same rows, so they retract the same ids -- the network one at a time, FireLoop as a batch -- and agree after; a phase that ends nothing, or ends rows that supported nothing alone, changes neither side.

idris.name: rlow_4_2_1__retract_ids_agree
idris.note: RETRACTING A BATCH OF IDS keeps the agreement: one at a time through alpha dispatch on the network, as a batch with one propagation on FireLoop. Each network retraction keeps the agreement against one more FireLoop propagation, and those propagations compose into the batch's one; an id no live fact carries retracts nothing on either side.

idris.name: iret_12_2__drop_pointwise_live
idris.note: Dropping a live id then the rest, member by member, is dropping the fact then the rest: ids are unique.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_cons_dead
idris.note: Retracting an id no live fact carries changes nothing.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_cons_live
idris.note: Retracting a live id and then the rest is retracting the rest from the memory less that fact: ids are unique, so the id names one fact.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_nil
idris.note: No ids: nothing retracted.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__prop_rule_shrink_compose
idris.note: The clause's 'for each' retraction, done one fact at a time as the reference engine does, ends where the batch does.

idris.name: rarc_5_6_5__propagate_shrink_compose
idris.note: The tables after the batch's one propagation are the tables after the facts' successive retractions.

idris.name: iret_12_2__elem_same
idris.note: Two id lists with the same members are the same membership test.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_quiet
idris.note: Phases on the network that end nothing touch nothing.

idris.name: iret_12_2__alphas_four
idris.note: Four alphas, kinds 0 to 3. A fixture.

idris.name: iret_12_2__queued_successor_removed_timed
idris.note: A FIRED `now()` MATCH WHOSE FACT A WITHDRAW REMOVES LOSES ITS JUSTIFICATION: the Reading at (0, 0) fires `fresh`, which emits Fresh; an advance to 1, a Kill and a pump: the re-time keeps `fresh`'s match (the gate is still open), `kill` fires first and withdraws the Reading, the match ends and Fresh is retracted with its one justification; a Probe and a pump: `live`, which joins Fresh with Probe, finds no Fresh and does not fire -- logical/IRET.12.2_queued_successor_removed_withdraws's shape. Executed: `[[(1, True)], [(0, True)], []]`, and working memory ends with the Kill and the Probe. LESS than the clause's PATH: the clause's successor activation on the agenda is this engine's one persisting activation, ended by the withdraw before the pump reaches it; the outcome is the clause's.

idris.name: iret_12_2__successor_life
idris.note: The lifecycles of the queued-successor fixture: Reading (0), Kill (1) and Probe (2) explicit, Fresh (3) a relation. A fixture.

idris.name: iret_12_2__successor_rules
idris.note: The three rules in source order: `kill` (a Kill and a Reading, withdraw the Reading), `fresh` (a Reading under `now() < 2`, emit Fresh logical), `live` (a Fresh and a Probe). A fixture.

idris.name: iret_12_2__successor_tests
idris.note: The tests by ordinal: `fresh` alone is timed. A fixture.

idris.name: Ltim_2_7_2__justified_only_by_ended
idris.note: The rows a phase ends, read per target id: every row targeting the id fails the clause's liveness test. The predicate under the frame of a lapse, not a restatement of `iret_12_2__ended_net`.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_net_wm_sub
idris.note: A CASCADE ONLY REMOVES FACTS: a fact in working memory after any number of phases was in it before. By induction on the phases, an ending phase being `iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_sub` and a quiet phase the identity.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_net_split
idris.note: ONE PHASE, BY CASES: it ends nothing and is the identity, or it ends rows and the engine it leaves is the retraction of the zeroed ids from the engine it started with. Rete/NetworkFrameClocked.idr's `iret_12_2__phase_step_net_shape` with the engine named rather than existential; the shape lemma's length bound is not restated.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_wm_eng
idris.note: Rete/NetworkTms.idr's `iret_12_2__retract_ids_net_wm` for an engine given whole, by matching the record. A wrapper.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__cascade_drops
idris.note: [IRET.12.2]'s step 3 as a theorem about the whole cascade: a fact whose every row has ended is retracted in the first phase and stays retracted, on the network's one-fact-at-a-time phase, for any fuel.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__dead_row_is_ended
idris.note: A row whose activation is not live is among the rows the phase ends, whatever its target's liveness: the ending test is `not (live && target_live)`.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__kept_count_zero
idris.note: A KEPT ROW TARGETS NO LAPSED ID: the id's `justif_count` against the rows the phase keeps is zero, because a kept row's activation is live and every row targeting the id has one that is not.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapse_only_dead
idris.note: EXECUTED: every row targeting the kind-2 fact has lapsed -- there is one, and it has.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__lapsed_justification_retracted
idris.note: The cascade after the re-time, on the clocked state: the clause's retraction of what an ended activation alone supported, proved for the re-time stage of every tick.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__retracted_at_the_fixture
idris.note: The cascade's retraction executed through the theorem at the fixture with one row to drop.

idris.name: ltim_2_7_2__zeroed_holds_it
idris.note: THE LAPSED ID IS ZEROED: when the phase ends rows, an id some row targets and every row of which has lapsed is among the ids the phase retracts -- it is a target of an ended row and its count against the kept rows is 0.

idris.name: iret_12_2__boundary_fixpoint
idris.note: AT A BOUNDARY, and at every state between actions, the live ids are exactly Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade of the engine's own table over themselves: every row is live, so the live set is self-supported, and the cascade is the greatest self-supported subset.

idris.name: iret_12_2__external_cascade
idris.note: A change of working memory outside any firing -- ids kept, at most facts with fresh ids added, unique, in the domain -- followed by propagation and the cascade keeps the run invariant and the target kinds: the bridge's premises hold because every row was live. It also reports that the cascade only removed facts and kept every explicit-kind fact.

idris.name: iret_12_2__external_entry
idris.note: The entry to that cascade: the bridge's cascade invariant holds over the rows and the ids live after the change, and the target kinds are kept. Split out so a caller can reach the invariant the cascade ends in.

idris.name: iret_12_2__external_final
idris.note: The cascade after such a change ends in the bridge's cascade invariant relative to the rows and the ids live after the change: rows drawn from them, a row with live antecedents and target kept, Refcount's cascade still live.

idris.name: iret_12_2__external_gfp
idris.note: So the cascade after such a change keeps Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade of the rows over the ids live after it: the half of the bridge a caller needs to show that a fact survives.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_explicit
idris.note: A cascade phase never removes a fact of an explicit kind: what it retracts is a row's target, and a row's target is `logical`. What Rete/TtlSweep.idr needs to keep a TTL fact through a sweep.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_facts_sub
idris.note: A cascade phase only removes facts.

idris.name: iret_12_2__base_shrink
idris.note: A base fact still live after a retraction is still base: the rows are the same.

idris.name: iret_12_2__base_sub_rows
idris.note: A base fact stays base when rows are dropped and it is still live.

idris.name: iret_12_2__elem_agree
idris.note: The two membership tests on ids agree.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_cascade
idris.note: Retracting a list of ids is an external change in Rete/PumpBoundary.idr's sense, so the cascade after it keeps the run invariant and the target kinds, only removes facts, and keeps explicit-kind facts.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_final
idris.note: And that cascade ends in the bridge's cascade invariant relative to the rows and the ids that survived the retraction.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_gfp
idris.note: And that cascade keeps Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade of the rows over the ids that survived the retraction.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_inv
idris.note: A survivor of the retraction was live, and its id was not retracted.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_keeps
idris.note: A fact whose id is not retracted survives the retraction.

idris.name: iret_12_3__certified_ranked
idris.note: The clause's own sentence, on the engine, for the kind-level certificate: on every positive program certified over the kind graph, support is acyclic. At every state between actions of a run the table is ranked (a fact by one more than the highest stratum emitting its kind), so the count is exact there (Rete/Refcount.idr's iret_12_3__ranked_agree). What the count's correctness rests on, proved rather than argued -- `partial`, because a program [LCYC.3.1.1] admits only through [LCYC.6.1]'s literal break has no kind-level certificate and the theorem is silent on it.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_in_cascade_of
idris.note: The cascade keeps every well-founded fact over a smaller live set and a different base, provided the well-founded facts are live there and a base fact still live is still base. Generalises `llog_2_5__wf_in_cascade`.

idris.name: iret_12_2__hybrid_mixed_refcount
idris.note: Executed: a recursive stratum seeded from outside with a self-free stratum on top, the seed withdrawn; the refcount over both keeps all three facts -- 1 and 2 on each other, 5 on 1.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade
idris.note: The cascade to its fixpoint: what the refcount leaves live after a set of base retractions.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_closed
idris.note: A survivor is a base fact or is supported by the survivors.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_fixed
idris.note: The cascade's result is a fixpoint of the cascade step.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_greatest
idris.note: The cascade keeps every self-supported subset of the live set, so it is the GREATEST such set -- the exact sense in which [IRET.12.2]'s mechanism keeps an unfounded cycle alive.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_n
idris.note: Iterate the step; fuel = the number of live facts suffices, since a step that changes anything removes a fact.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_n_fixed
idris.note: The cascade stabilises within as many steps as there are live facts: a step that retracts nothing is the fixpoint, one that retracts something shortens the live list: the fuel the cascade is given always suffices.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_n_stable
idris.note: Once a step retracts nothing, no later step does.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_step
idris.note: Steps 1-3 for every ended activation at once: each live derived fact whose count is zero against the current live set is retracted. The engine does this incrementally; the fixpoint it reaches is the same.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_step_sub
idris.note: A cascade step only ever retracts.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_sub
idris.note: The cascade's result lies in the live set it started from.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_unfounded
idris.note: What the refcount keeps beyond the well-founded answer is an unfounded set: mutual support with nothing under it. The general form of what `iret_12_2__witness_refcount` and `iret_12_2__reach_refcount` exhibit on instances.

idris.name: iret_12_2__reach_refcount
idris.note: Executed on the `+recursive` proposal's own shape (seed -> Reach(a,b); Reach + Edge derives Reach(a,a); that re-derives Reach(a,b)): withdrawing the seed leaves both Reach facts live under the refcount.

idris.name: iret_12_2__strata_refcount
idris.note: Executed: two recursive strata, seed withdrawn; the cascade keeps all four derived facts, the upper cycle through a lower-stratum fact that is itself unfounded.

idris.name: iret_12_2__tla_retract_both
idris.note: Executed: after both base facts are retracted the cascade and the well-founded answer agree (everything goes).

idris.name: iret_12_2__tla_retract_f1
idris.note: Executed on tms_cascade.tla's ranked instance: after f1 is retracted the cascade and the well-founded answer agree.

idris.name: iret_12_2__unfounded_base_free
idris.note: A survivor outside the well-founded set is not a base fact.

idris.name: iret_12_2__unfounded_held
idris.note: A justification keeping a survivor outside the well-founded set alive has an antecedent outside it too.

idris.name: iret_12_2__witness_refcount
idris.note: Executed: rules P -> Q, Q -> R, R -> Q, retract P. The cascade retracts nothing -- Q and R each keep a live justifier in the other -- although no base fact founds either. The count, applied exactly as written, leaves an unfounded cycle live. Well-founded is the contract; this clause states it and keeps the count as libds's mechanism, correct because [LCYC.3.1.1] makes support acyclic, so no admitted program reaches this witness.

idris.name: iret_12_3__ranked_agree
idris.note: Both inclusions on a ranked graph: the cascade and the well-founded set contain each other.

idris.name: iret_12_3__ranked_exact
idris.note: On a ranked (acyclic) support graph every survivor of the cascade is well-founded -- the refcount is exact there.

idris.name: llog_2_5__wf_in_cascade
idris.note: The cascade never retracts a well-founded fact: the well-founded set is self-supported, so the greatest self-supported set contains it. Generalises `iret_12_2__cascade_step_keeps`.

idris.name: Iret_12_2__cascade_inv
idris.note: The cascade invariant, relative to the starting table and live set: the core invariant and unique ids; rows and live ids drawn from the start; every starting row still a match; a starting row whose antecedents are all live is present, live, with its target live; Refcount's cascade of the starting reading still live; every live non-base fact has a row.

idris.name: iret_12_2__any_true
idris.note: A true `any` exhibits its witness.

idris.name: iret_12_2__base
idris.note: The live facts no row justifies: never retracted by the cascade. Refcount's base, read off the engine's table.

idris.name: iret_12_2__base_row
idris.note: At the start a live fact outside the base has a row targeting it.

idris.name: iret_12_2__bridge
idris.note: THE BRIDGE THEOREM. On a positive program, from a settled state with unique ids whose live rows read as matches and whose rows with live antecedents and a live target are live activations, the cascade reaches a phase that ends nothing within its fuel, and the ids live there are exactly Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade of the engine's own table over the ids live at the start with the never-justified ones as base. Both inclusions and the fixpoint. With Rete/Refcount.idr's theorems the engine's retraction is the greatest self-supported subset of the live set, and what it keeps beyond the well-founded answer is an unfounded set. The premises are what a state satisfies between actions; that every run's states satisfy them is the engine-level invariant of the next increment.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_not_zeroed
idris.note: THE KEY STEP. A fact of Refcount's cascade is never zeroed by a phase: base, and then no row targets it while an ended one does; or supported in the cascade, and the supporting row's antecedents are live, so it is a kept activation and the count is not zero. `iret_12_2__cascade_closed` from Rete/Refcount.idr does the work.

idris.name: iret_12_2__drop_preserves
idris.note: A phase that ends activations but zeroes nothing keeps the invariant with the surviving rows.

idris.name: iret_12_2__elem_concat_map
idris.note: Membership through `concat_map`.

idris.name: iret_12_2__filter_drops
idris.note: A filter that drops a member is strictly shorter: the pigeonhole the fuel rests on.

idris.name: iret_12_2__filter_lte
idris.note: A filter is no longer than its input.

idris.name: iret_12_2__fixed_post
idris.note: At a phase that ends nothing every live fact is base or supported among the live facts by a row's activation, whose token is a current match of live facts: the live set is self-supported, which is what `iret_12_2__cascade_greatest` needs.

idris.name: iret_12_2__is_live_before
idris.note: A target live after a retraction was live before.

idris.name: iret_12_2__live_before
idris.note: An id live after a retraction was live before.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_after_eta
idris.note: Whatever a phase retracts, its rows are the kept ones.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_after_preserves
idris.note: The two outcomes of a phase that ended something, each keeping the invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_fixed
idris.note: THE FUEL: with at least as many phases as rows the cascade reaches a phase that ends nothing, since every other phase drops a row. What `iret_12_2__phase` relies on, proved.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_preserves
idris.note: And so does any number of phases.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_stable
idris.note: Nothing ending, nothing changes however many phases run.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_succ
idris.note: One more phase, when the first is known.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_preserves
idris.note: PRESERVATION: one phase keeps the invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_nil
idris.note: A phase that ends nothing is the identity.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_step_shape
idris.note: A phase either ends nothing and is the identity, or keeps strictly fewer rows: the ended row is dropped.

idris.name: iret_12_2__retract_preserves
idris.note: A phase that retracts keeps the invariant: the core invariant by `lcyc_1_1__propagate_inv`, uniqueness and the row readings through the filter, the live activations by the token lemma `iret_7_8__live_after_propagate`, the cascade by `iret_12_2__cascade_not_zeroed`.

idris.name: iret_12_2__survives
idris.note: A live fact whose id is not retracted survives the retraction.

idris.name: iret_12_2__survives_inv
idris.note: A survivor was live, with an id not retracted.

idris.name: iret_12_2__target_kept
idris.note: A row targeting a fact, after the endings: kept, or ended with the fact not zeroed and then some kept row targets it -- step 3 read backwards.

idris.name: iret_12_2__action_cascade
idris.note: AT EVERY ACTION OF EVERY RUN, THE BRIDGE APPLIES. One action with truth maintenance from a state satisfying the firing invariant: the core action gives the new working memory and tables, the record gives the table, and the cascade from there ends in a state whose live ids are exactly Rete/Refcount.idr's cascade of that table over the ids live after the action, with the never-justified ones as base. Both inclusions, and the firing invariant holds again.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_entry
idris.note: THE CASCADE ENTRY. After a core action and its record, from a state satisfying the firing invariant, the bridge's premises hold: every live row reads as a match, every row whose antecedents and target are live is live, and the firing activation is still tracked.

idris.name: iret_12_2__cascade_tracked
idris.note: THE BRIDGE WITH A TRACKED ACTIVATION: the bridge's cascade, whose final state satisfies the cascade invariant and ends nothing, keeps a tracked activation tracked.

idris.name: iret_12_2__entry_live_after
idris.note: A live activation whose antecedents stay live is live after the action's propagation, if any.

idris.name: iret_12_2__entry_live_before
idris.note: A live activation after the action's propagation, if any, was live before.

idris.name: iret_12_2__entry_read_old
idris.note: An old row live before the action reads as a match in the new working memory: its ids were all live, so no added fact carries one of them.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_after_core_shape
idris.note: What the end of a phase does to the core state: nothing, or a retraction and its propagation.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_core_shape
idris.note: What a phase does to the core state: nothing, or a retraction and its propagation.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_tracked
idris.note: And so does any number of phases, alongside the cascade invariant.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_tracked
idris.note: One phase keeps a tracked activation.

idris.name: iret_12_2__phase_n_facts_sub
idris.note: The cascade only removes facts, over any number of phases.

tla.name: iret_12_2__no_unsupported_forever
tla.note: The count's mechanism as a cascade, on the ranked instance tms_cascade.cfg selects (f2 <- {f1}, f2 <- {f4}, f3 <- {f2}; `iret_12__GRAPH`): a derived fact whose every justification has lost an antecedent is retracted, and what the cascade leaves is the greatest self-supported set below the live facts, `formal/idris/Rete/Refcount.idr`'s `iret_12_2__cascade`. On acyclic support that is the clause's obligation (`iret_12_3__ranked_agree`), and `iret_12_2__tla_retract_f1` and `_both` execute the agreement on this instance, which `formal/checks/check_instances.py` (`instances.stamp`) holds equal to the module's on every run of the lane. Of cyclic support, where the obligation and the mechanism part (`iret_12_2__witness_refcount`: rules P -> Q, Q -> R, R -> Q, retract P; the count keeps Q and R live, the well-founded set drops them), this property says nothing: on the cycle its antecedent is never true, and `iret_12_2__quiescent_is_well_founded` is what the `.teeth.cycle.` run violates there. Well-founded support is the contract ([LLOG.2.5]), so `partial` stands.
